cards.explanation: The answer is a man carrying a jug of water. Jesus says, “Go into the city, and a man carrying a jug of water will meet you. Follow him…” and that's the whole sign. No name, no address, just a guy and a jug. I'd have asked for a second clue, friends. But verse 16 says the disciples found everything as Jesus had described.

The answer is a large upper room. Jesus says the owner “…will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready.” Big, upstairs, and already set up. That's a host who thought of everything. I can't even find my own rolling pin half the time, friends.
The answer is False. Mark 14:16 says the disciples left, went into the city and found everything as Jesus had described. Then they prepared the Passover. Every detail He gave them lined up.

The answer is that one of them will betray Him. Jesus says, “Truly I tell you, one of you who is eating with Me will betray Me.” He says it while they're reclining and eating together. That's a hard thing to say across a dinner table. I think the room got very quiet, friends.
The answer is grieved. Mark 14:19 says they “…began to be grieved…” Then they ask Him one after another, “Surely not I?” I think grief fits, friends, when the news is about someone at your own table.
The answer is False. Jesus says, “It is one of the Twelve—the one who is dipping his hand into the bowl with Me.” So the betrayer is someone inside the circle, at that very table.

The answer is that it would be better for him if he had never been born. Jesus says, “…woe to that man by whom He is betrayed! It would be better for him if he had not been born.” I think this one is heavy, and it should be. He also says the Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him. Take that line slowly, friends.
The answer is body. As He hands the bread to the disciples, Jesus says, “Take it; this is My body.” They are eating together when He says it. That's a moment to hold quietly, friends.

The answer is His blood of the covenant. Jesus says, “This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.” He gives them the cup and says what it is. They all drank from it. It's one of the most serious things He says at that table.

The answer is in the kingdom of God. Jesus says, “…I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in the kingdom of God.” Notice the word anew. He's talking about a day still ahead. That's the kind of line that keeps my ovens warm and ready, friends.

The answer is that they will all fall away. On the Mount of Olives, Jesus tells them, “You will all fall away…” He points to what is written: “I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.” It's a hard thing to hear from Him. And the word is all, not some.

The answers are risen and Galilee. Jesus says, “But after I have risen…” Right after the hard news about the scattering, He says what comes after. That one little word gives the whole line its hope, friends. Jesus says, “…I will go ahead of you into Galilee.” He doesn't just say He'll come back. He says He goes ahead of them. That's a promise with a destination.

The answer is that Peter will deny Him three times. Jesus tells Peter, one of the Twelve, “this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” That's both the number and the timing, and Jesus doesn't leave it vague. Peter has just said he never will. Ouch, friends.
The answer is False. Peter kept insisting, “Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.” He says it after Jesus has just told him what will happen. He was holding his ground, friends.
The answer is False. Mark 14:31 says, “And all the others said the same thing.” So Peter isn't alone in what he says. The other disciples say it right along with him.
